data.name: CanceledMessage
data.value: The statement was canceled.

data.name: UnknownOutcomeAdvice
data.value: Prism does not know whether the statement finished: check the database before running it again.

data.name: UnknownOutcomeMessage
data.value: The database did not answer the cancellation in time, and the session was closed. {0}

data.name: CanceledWhileReturningRowsMessage
data.value: The cancellation arrived while the statement was returning the rows. What it wrote up to that point is confirmed, and it may be only part of the statement: Prism does not know whether it finished. Check the database before running it again.

data.name: ConnectionClosedMessage
data.value: The connection to the database was closed, and the statement was not sent. Open the session again.

data.name: NoOpenCursorMessage
data.value: There is no open cursor: run the statement again.

data.name: UnknownObjectKindMessage
data.value: The requested object type does not exist: use tables, views, routines or sequences.

data.name: TransactionControlMessage
data.value: Transaction control statements (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT) are not accepted in Auto-commit, where each statement is committed when it finishes. To control the transaction, choose "Manual commit" in the editor bar: the first statement opens the transaction, and "Commit" and "Rollback" (or COMMIT and ROLLBACK typed) end it.

data.name: NeverTransactionControlMessage
data.value: Two-phase commit (PREPARE TRANSACTION, COMMIT PREPARED), AND CHAIN, and COMMIT or ROLLBACK followed by anything else are not accepted; nothing was sent. Use COMMIT or ROLLBACK alone, or the "Commit" and "Rollback" buttons.

data.name: NotAllowedInTransactionMessage
data.value: This statement does not run inside a transaction, and the database's refusal would spoil the tab's manual transaction; nothing was sent. Run it in a tab in Auto-commit.

data.name: ReadOnlyWithTransactionMessage
data.value: The connection became read-only with a manual transaction open in this tab; nothing was sent. End the transaction with "Commit" or "Rollback" first.

data.name: RollbackWorkToSavepointMessage
data.value: With the IBM driver, ROLLBACK WORK TO SAVEPOINT undoes the whole transaction, not just what came after the savepoint; nothing was sent. Write ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, without the WORK.

data.name: CanceledWhileReturningRowsInTransactionMessage
data.value: The cancellation arrived while the statement was returning the rows. What it wrote up to that point stayed in the transaction, without a commit, and it may be only part of the statement: Prism does not know whether it finished. Check before the Commit.

data.name: UndoneTransactionMessage
data.value: The statement left a transaction open, and Prism rolled it back: nothing it wrote inside it stayed. {0}

data.name: WritesAfterTheFirstPageMessage
data.value: The statement started as a read and tried to write after the first page; nothing was written. Run it again: it will run to the end.

data.name: SeveralStatementsMessage
data.value: Each run takes a single statement, and the text sent has more than one; nothing was run. Send one at a time. A block with `;` in the body (procedure, function, trigger, compound block) is a single statement.

data.name: NotCountableMessage
data.value: Only a read can be counted, and the statement sent is not a single read; nothing was run.

data.name: NoRowMessage
data.value: The row no longer exists, or its key changed: the statement did not change any row.

data.name: IsolationLevelInvalid
data.value: The isolation level "{0}" does not exist for this database.

data.name: TransactionOpenForIsolation
data.value: The tab has an open transaction: end it with Commit or Rollback before changing the isolation level.

data.name: NoTransactionLogForIsolation
data.value: This database has no transaction log: the only isolation level available is Dirty Read.

data.name: EditWouldChangeMany
data.value: The statement would change {0} rows, not just one.

data.name: CountReturnedNoRow
data.value: The count returned no row.

data.name: SemicolonInHost
data.value: The IBM driver does not accept `;` in the host: it is the character it uses to separate the connection data.

data.name: SemicolonInPassword
data.value: The IBM driver does not accept `;` in the password: it is the character it uses to separate the connection data.

data.name: SemicolonInDatabase
data.value: The IBM driver does not accept `;` in the database name: it is the character it uses to separate the connection data.

data.name: SemicolonInUserName
data.value: The IBM driver does not accept `;` in the user: it is the character it uses to separate the connection data.

data.name: VariableQueryTooManyColumns
data.value: A variable's query has up to {0} columns, and this one has {1}.

data.name: VariableQueryTooManyRows
data.value: A variable's query reads up to {0} rows, and this one returned more.

data.name: VariableQueryTooManyBytes
data.value: The values of a variable's query go over 16 MiB.
